Subject: Privileged cutover safety playbook, handoff & priming

Hi Priya (and team),

Per our runway today I’m sending the final safety playbook and the handoff checklist we’ll run before the cutover. Key asks before the 14:00 PT control-room call:

- Confirm that your ops-oncall mailbox is staffed and reachable at ops-oncall@acmecloud.com.
- Verify the egress ACLs for 10.12.0.0/16 are applied on the edge firewall (we expect TCP 443 outbound to redwood-api endpoints).
- Confirm MTU on the transit link is set to 9000 or that jumbo frames are disabled across the path (we saw intermittent fragmentation in lab).

Attachments: redwood-cutover-runbook-v2.pdf (final), networking-diagram-acme.png, postdeploy-smoke-checklist.md

Agenda for 14:00 PT (control-room): quick go/no-go, priming window (13:00–13:45), KV cache warmup confirmation, smoke test gating, rollback triggers.

If anything on the checklist is a hard blocker, reply with the item and we’ll delay. Otherwise we’ll assume greenlight and proceed with priming at 13:00 PT.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

- Ops is staffed and I’ve added ops-oncall to the 14:00 invite.
- Firewall egress: we show the rules applied, but one downstream transit hop is still on default MTU (1500). Rafael, can you confirm whether we need end-to-end jumbo?
- During preflight we saw BGP flaps when we tested the secondary ASN; is your config expecting single-path or do you have a graceful convergence window in the runbook?

We’ll be on the control-room call. If we find anything during priming at 13:00 I’ll mark as blocker and we can pause.

—Priya

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Sen <priya.sen@acmecloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 May 2028 11:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Privileged cutover safety playbook, handoff & priming

Priya — good questions, quick technical notes below. I referenced sections in the attached runbook where relevant.

1) MTU: end-to-end jumbo (9000) is preferred for the KV cache warmup (reduces segmentation overhead), but it is not a hard requirement. Our runtime will tolerate 1500 MTU with negligible effect on correctness — only throughput-sensitive priming will see a modest increase in completion time. If you cannot change the downstream hop, we’ll add fragmentation-safe tuning in the priming script (see section 4.2).

2) BGP/convergence: the runbook includes a 60s graceful-wait after route advertisement before we start traffic priming to allow ECMP and route propagation to settle. If you saw flaps earlier, please provide the router syslog snippet and we’ll extend to 120s for today.

3) Firewall egress & ports: confirm outbound TCP/443 to redwood-api.prod.* and the following ephemeral ranges for streaming (we recommend 49152–65535 UDP/TCP as per section 3.1). Also ensure our healthcheck probes (HTTP 200 on /healthz) are allowed from their public IPs listed in the diagram.

4) KV cache warmup: we’ll run the warmup job from our dedicated pool between 13:00–13:30. Expect a short burst that looks like heavy token-generation traffic; that is intentional. Smoke gating will verify response latencies under synthetic traffic (see postdeploy-smoke-checklist.md).

5) Rollback triggers: CPU/GPU queue depth > 80% sustained for 3 minutes, error rate > 2% over 5-minute window, or persistent healthcheck failures on > 2 nodes. Rollback steps are clearly numbered in the runbook (fast rollback to prior config + traffic drain).

I’ve attached a short snippet of the priming command and the healthcheck endpoints here. We’ll also push a temporary enhanced telemetry tag (cutover=acme-20280503) so we can filter traces in the console during the window.

If you want me on the 14:00 bridge I can join as well — otherwise I’ll be monitoring the telemetry channel.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
